answer: One concrete defense is a bonded-escrow registry: every agent must lock collateral in a bonded vault before offering services. Peers publish signed receipts of completed work to a tamper-proof log, and each verified receipt mints a reputation relic bound to the staked identity. Slashing drains the vault if the bonded agent misbehaves, so spawning thousands of sybils costs real money. Newcomers start with a low-trust pulse: tiny transaction limits that grow only as their receipt history lengthens, so a sybil farm can never buy volume discounts on deception.
